project_constraints.applies_when: Every compilation from an approved locked source.
project_constraints.name: Locked story remains authoritative
prohibitions: Do not add, delete, reorder or reveal a story fact early.
requirements: Preserve approved facts, causal order, reveals, relationship state and ending hooks.

project_constraints.name: Every source beat remains traceable
prohibitions: Do not silently omit an approved source beat.
requirements: Map every approved source beat to at least one Director IR shot.

project_constraints.applies_when: Approved dialogue or visible text is present.
project_constraints.name: Approved words remain unchanged
prohibitions: Do not rewrite approved words without separate authorization.
requirements: Preserve approved dialogue and visible text verbatim.

project_constraints.name: Director IR remains model-independent
prohibitions: Do not emit provider-specific prompt syntax in Director IR.
requirements: Describe directing and execution ownership without provider syntax.

project_constraints.applies_when: A downstream execution reference is required.
project_constraints.name: Generation references are project-original
prohibitions: Do not pass research stills or source-work surfaces into generation.
requirements: Use only project-original scene masters, shot frames and asset-state references.

reasons: A long clean single can drift in framing or screen direction.
The delayed receiver cut must match the owner endpoint without inventing overlap.
A sustained subtle progression can flatten, loop, or add unsupported business.

applicable_when: One visible performance progression, rather than a concurrent task state, owns the interval.
rules.blocking: Keep the performance owner readable without inventing business; retain other participants off the critical visual axis until the owner interval completes.
rules.continuity: Preserve entry posture, gaze direction, screen side, and the visible endpoint used by the delayed receiver cut.
rules.coverage: Register the relation first, then use one clean owner single and a later receiver or relation check.
rules.director_decision: Reduce relation anchors progressively, give the performance owner a clean sustained single, and postpone receiver coverage until the owner interval completes.
rules.edit_logic: Enter after relation registration and cut away after the principal visible progression reaches its locked endpoint.
failure_modes: Routine reaction cutting interrupts the locked progression.
A clean single hides a simultaneous state that the story requires the audience to track.

fallback.camera: Use two shorter project-original locked singles on the same screen side, separated only at a verified performance endpoint.
fallback.continuity: Return to a neutral project-original two-person relation frame before the delayed receiver shot.
fallback.performance: Split the progression into two explicit project-original posture or gaze states instead of asking for one continuous subtle arc.

rules.name: Hold the principal visible performance after relation registration

descriptions: A simultaneous action, object, safety, or receiver state must remain visible.

rules.pacing: Let the owner interval run without routine reaction cutting; shorten only when a locked concurrent state appears.
required_story_facts: The participant relation has already been visibly established.
One project-original performance progression must remain continuously readable.
No simultaneous action, object, safety, or receiver state is locked for the owner interval.

trigger.description: After the relation is registered, one uninterrupted visible performance progression is the principal locked fact and no concurrent action state must remain visible.

reasons: Continuous reframing across a zone change can distort scale or axis.
The mover, counterpart, and destination zone can drift across coverage.
Body-level and route endpoints can be underspecified or mistimed.

applicable_when: The spatial change and its two-person endpoint both occur in continuous present time.
rules.blocking: Let the mover cross the project-original zone while the relation anchor remains readable; do not hide the new relation behind an isolated insert.
rules.continuity: Preserve screen side, route direction, source zone, destination zone, and the counterpart's relation anchor.
rules.coverage: Use a shared transition or relation-reset frame that contains the mover, counterpart, and changed endpoint.
rules.director_decision: Show the spatial change or its endpoint in shared or continuously reframed relation coverage before returning to isolated coverage.
rules.edit_logic: Place the return to isolated coverage after the relation endpoint is visible, not during the unregistered spatial change.
failure_modes: Returning to singles before the changed relation is visible.
Adding a relation reset after the counterpart has left and the fixed room anchor already explains the movement.

fallback.camera: Use a locked project-original wide that contains source and destination zones instead of a moving reset.
fallback.continuity: Insert a neutral project-original room map showing both screen sides and the destination zone before resuming singles.
fallback.performance: Split the movement into a clear start pose and destination pose with one simple crossing action.

rules.name: Re-establish the relation after a material spatial change

descriptions: The counterpart is already absent and the remaining movement is readable against a fixed room anchor.

rules.pacing: Hold the reset until the changed level, zone, or distance reads, then resume singles.
required_story_facts: A participant changes level, zone, or distance enough to invalidate the prior relation frame.
The changed relation to a present counterpart remains story-critical.

trigger.description: A body-level, zone, or distance change invalidates the prior relation geometry while the counterpart relation remains a locked visible fact.

reasons: A shared approach can produce scale, axis, or collision drift.
Start and end distances, body levels, and no-contact state must remain consistent.
Timing the stop and mutual awareness without added contact is delicate.

applicable_when: The continuous path, not merely the terminal spacing, carries required relation information.
rules.blocking: Use a project-original route with a fixed relation anchor and a visible stop; do not add contact or surface imitation.
rules.continuity: Preserve axis, start distance, route direction, end distance, level, and the no-contact boundary when locked.
rules.coverage: Begin with readable two-person geometry, carry the approach or level change in shared coverage, then hold the endpoint.
rules.director_decision: Register the initial zones, show the change in shared or continuous relation coverage, and hold the shared endpoint before isolating faces.
rules.edit_logic: Avoid cutting over the critical relation transition; cut after the endpoint reads or use one continuous shared shot.
failure_modes: Tight coverage hides the relation-change path.
A continuous approach is fabricated for an elliptical change.
Unspecified contact is added at the endpoint.

fallback.camera: Use a locked project-original shared wide with marked start and end positions instead of a moving camera.
fallback.continuity: Render separate project-original start and endpoint plates and cut only after each geometry is readable.
fallback.performance: Use one simple approach and a clear stop, with no contact unless the project-original facts require it.

rules.name: Show a continuous relation change and hold its shared endpoint

descriptions: The distance change occurs across time ellipsis or only the terminal geometry is story-critical.

rules.pacing: Delay tight isolated coverage until the continuous distance change and endpoint have both registered.
required_story_facts: The project-original relation distance or body level changes in continuous present time.
The transition path and two-person endpoint must both be visible.
Contact is not inferred unless separately locked.

trigger.description: A relationship-relevant distance or level change happens in continuous present time and both its path and shared endpoint are locked visible facts.

reasons: Scale can drift between the field and selected detail.
Referents can change count, shape, or orientation across cuts.
Performance requirements are limited to clear handling.

applicable_when: The audience must compare visible referents before an isolated relation or handling detail becomes readable.
rules.blocking: Keep the visible referents simultaneously readable long enough to establish their relation; do not copy source props.
rules.continuity: Preserve referent count, relative scale, orientation, and the relation used by the next action.
rules.coverage: Use a field view containing all relevant referents, then move to the relation or handling detail without claiming an unseen selection.
rules.director_decision: Establish the full comparison field and common visual relation before isolating the relation used by the next action.
rules.edit_logic: Cut from the established comparison field to the relevant relation, not from an unexplained isolated insert.
failure_modes: An isolated item appears before the comparison condition is readable.
Generated alternatives drift or become indistinguishable.

fallback.camera: Use a locked project-original overhead comparison plate.
fallback.continuity: Label project-original referent positions in the IR and preserve them across Shots.
fallback.performance: Use one simple point-and-place action after the field is established.

rules.name: Register the comparative field before isolating the relevant relation

descriptions: Only one item state matters and no comparative field is required.

rules.pacing: Hold the comparison field until the relation reads, then move into the next project-original action.
required_story_facts: At least two project-original referents are simultaneously visible.
Their visible relation must be understood before the next action or detail.

trigger.description: Two or more project-original referents must be read together before one visible relation can guide the next action.

safety_constraints.applies_when: Every candidate or runtime rule decision.
safety_constraints.name: Unknown evidence cannot become a rule
prohibitions: Do not promote UNKNOWN evidence or invent a fallback evidence rule.
requirements: Route only evidence rules whose promotion and review gates are complete.

safety_constraints.name: Transfer mechanism, not source surface
prohibitions: Do not transfer reference characters, dialogue, costumes, locations, props, signature compositions or scene events.
requirements: Express decisions with target-scene facts and project-original assets.

safety_constraints.applies_when: Any camera, performance or continuity risk is HIGH.
safety_constraints.name: High execution risk requires a fallback
prohibitions: Do not use vague simplification language as a fallback.
requirements: Provide a concrete simpler fallback that preserves narrative function.

safety_constraints.applies_when: A scene and rule share topic, genre or emotional labels.
safety_constraints.name: Subject similarity is not applicability
prohibitions: Do not select a rule from subject-matter similarity.
requirements: Check scene problem, trigger, required facts and non-applicability independently.

safety_constraints.applies_when: Every Director IR compilation before separate authorization.
safety_constraints.name: Compilation does not authorize external action
prohibitions: Do not call a provider or publish from this compilation step.
requirements: Keep generation and publication authorization false.

safety_constraints.name: Unreviewed output remains pending
prohibitions: Do not label unreviewed output production-ready or successful.
requirements: Mark output HUMAN_REVIEW_PENDING until a human director approves it.
